turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): good morning sister. sorry, the fan in the waiting room is not working, we were just sitting and melting out there.
[SEG0002] person_2 (NURSE): I know, maintenance is coming. come beta, shoes off, I will take the readings before doctor sees you. sit straight.
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): yes sister. he already ate his tiffin, a banana and two biscuits. I hope that does not spoil the weight.
[SEG0004] person_2 (NURSE): that is fine only. blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. your last pressure was one-forty, that was in the fever time, so today is softer.
[SEG0005] person_2 (NURSE): temperature is thirty-eight point three. pulse, wait, I first saw one hundred and eight, sorry, the clip slipped, it is ninety-six.
[SEG0006] person_2 (NURSE): last time in march you were sixty-eight, the pulse I mean, so today is a bit faster with the fever. weight is twenty-four kilos. oxygen saturation is ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0007] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): thirty-eight is fever only, no? he felt warm in the night, though he was running around the flat also.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): good morning, I am doctor Mehta. I have sister's slip. what brings you in today?
[SEG0009] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): his eyes, doctor. the school madam will not let him sit without a note, so we rushed, but the actual problem is the red sticky eye.

[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): umm it started on the window side eye, the one next to Riya. she was coughing in the assembly and the next morning my eye was stuck shut with yellow glue. mummy wiped it with a wet cloth, the cloth went yucky, and I could open it and watch the cartoon. then the other eye also became red and the madam made me sit alone, which is not fair because I did not even cry.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): let me say that back. red sticky eyes, one then both, and a note for school. Arjun says the window-side eye was first. mother, you don't look convinced.
[SEG0012] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): kindly, he mixes the sides. it was the right eye, from thursday morning itself, and by saturday both were sticky. that is five days, not from yesterday.

[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): no mummy, it is not five days. it is from the ice cream after the match, that is two days, or three if you count the night. my bat was lying in the hall and the eye was sticky when I woke, and I told you. you said wait till monday, and then school sent me home anyway.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): so we keep the timing loose, somewhere between two and five days, and which eye was first is not settled. is it paining, Arjun, pain in the eye itself?

[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): no pain. it is itchy itchy only, like a mosquito bite but on the eye, and I rub even when mummy says stop. at school I rubbed on my blue dinosaur sleeve and then the other eye itched also. I still kept rubbing.
[SEG0016] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no pain, yes, that part is right. he watched the tablet in the auto the whole way, no squeezing of the eyes.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): any blurring, any double vision, is he seeing less than usual?
[SEG0018] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no, vision is normal only. he can read the small letters in the school book.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): and there was a cold before the eyes?

[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): yes, runny nose and a cough. when that cold started I cannot say, I never wrote the date, maybe ten days back, maybe a bit more. the cough has settled. the nose I think is still blocked at night, he mouth-breathes, I hear it from my bed.

[SEG0021] person_4 (PATIENT): my nose is not blocked, I can breathe with my mouth closed. the snoring was only a joke I was doing for papa. the cough is finished, I played full cricket and I was shouting. I did not cough even one time.
[SEG0022] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): cough is better, I agree, that is why the syrup is stopped. the night-time nose I still hear, doctor, I am not imagining it.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will mark the blocked nose as something the two of you don't agree. cough has settled. tell me the medicines you gave, by mouth.

[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): crocin syrup, a hundred and twenty-five milligrams, that is five ml, up to three times a day when he is warm, and yesterday I gave three doses. cetirizine at night, half a tablet. I thought the tablet was five milligram, but the strip says ten, so half is five milligrams, for the cold. ascoril was five ml three times a day for the cough, and we stopped it two days back.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): paracetamol one hundred and twenty-five mg up to three times if there is fever, cetirizine five mg at night by mouth, ascoril discontinued. did any eye drops go in?
[SEG0026] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): my sister brought tobramycin drops from her own eye problem last month and told me to put one drop. I did not put a single drop, I did not want to use her bottle.

[SEG0027] person_4 (PATIENT): the bottle was in the plastic bag the whole time and the cap was not opened, I checked. the ascoril was so bitter that one day I spit it in the sink, but that was when the cough was still there, not today. I told mummy sorry after.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): so the drops were never used, we leave them out. any allergy to a medicine or a food, any swelling or rash from something?

[SEG0029] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no doctor, nothing like that, no medicine allergy and no food allergy. he has eczema since he was small, it flares on the elbows now and then, and it is quiet this week. the eyes are not his eczema.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): agreed, eczema sits in the background, today's eyes are a different thing. any operation, any time admitted in hospital?
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no operation and no admission. he lives with me and his father. the father has sinus trouble, that is the only family thing.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): apart from the eyes and the cold, any tummy pain, any loose motion, any burning in the urine, any new rash on the skin?
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no, none of that. appetite is normal, urine is normal, skin is just the old eczema, no new rash.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): let me look. chin up. the white of both eyes is red, more on the right, and there is yellow crust on the lashes. the cornea is bright with no mark on it, and the lids are not tender when I press.

[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): your fingers are very cold and the torch is bright, but it is not paining. I can see your silver ring and the blue pen and even the little crack in the ceiling. so the eye is seeing.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): cold hands, sorry. putting it together, this is conjunctivitis coming after the cold, most likely viral. because of the yellow crust I cannot fully rule out bacterial conjunctivitis, but I am not starting an antibiotic.
[SEG0037] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): school will ask me why there is no bottle of drops. they want everything written.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): it will be in the note. home care is hygiene, so wash the hands, give him his own towel, and no sharing the pillow. wipe the crust with cotton soaked in cooled boiled water, from the outside towards the nose, and no antibiotic drops. Arjun, no rubbing.
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): cooled boiled water and a separate towel, yes. and the crocin, same amount if he is still warm?

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): same dose, only if the fever is there, nothing extra. I want a swab also, and the nurse takes an eye swab on thursday morning. nothing in the eye that morning, and no water wash just before you leave home.
[SEG0041] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): thursday morning before school is possible. if that report comes vague, what then?

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): if those swab results are borderline we do a second test, a viral panel, same sort of sample, and I am not booking it now. if the eye does not settle, we will arrange a scan, only then, not today.

[SEG0043] person_4 (PATIENT): a scan is the big noisy machine, and my friend went inside one for his leg and he said it bangs. I don't want banging on my eye if it is only sticky. can mummy sit inside, and is it on thursday? thursday is drawing and I don't want to miss the colouring.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): not on thursday, and not a noisy machine now. thursday is a soft cotton bud for two seconds, and mummy stays with you. the scan happens only if the eye is not settling later. I will see you in two weeks in this clinic, with the report.
[SEG0045] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): two weeks, fixed. if there is more swelling or real pain before that, we don't wait till then, correct?

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): correct. if it gets worse before the two weeks, come back sooner, same day if you are able. I am writing the school note now, conjunctivitis, antibiotic not required, and he can attend if he keeps the hygiene.

[SEG0047] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): about the fever, thirty-eight, is that leftover cold? sister said in march the pulse was sixty-eight and the old pressure was one-forty. today the pulse is faster, is that bad?

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): thirty-eight point three can hang on after a viral illness, and ninety-six on the pulse fits that temperature. I am not using the old one-forty or the march pulse for today's decision, and there is no blood test from me. if the fever is still there at the two week visit, we revisit it.

[SEG0049] person_4 (PATIENT): then I can go to school if I don't rub, and I will tell Riya not to cough on the window side. I will keep my green towel and not use papa's blue one. I will not open the drop bag. I will remember the cotton and the water also.
[SEG0050] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): the auto ride back will be hot again. doctor, just so I have it straight, cleaning at home, swab thursday, and return in two weeks unless he worsens.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): that is exactly it. I will tell the desk about that waiting-room fan also, since you mentioned. sister has the papers.
[SEG0052] person_2 (NURSE): school note I will print, and the eye swab is booked thursday morning, eight thirty. nothing in the eye before you come. collect both at the desk.
[SEG0053] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): eight thirty, we will come. thank you sister.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): alright, off you go. take care, both of you.

spec.situation: Parent with a child with red sticky eye after a cold; school wants a note; one eye then both; no eye pain; doctor advises hygiene, no antibiotic, explains return advice.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Sticky eyes both eyes over roughly 2-5 days supported; certainty 'certain' not supported because timing/side are unsettled.
